why_angle: The cited rivals (Watt & Warden, Power Station Field Guide, StorageReview) mark every single-box split-phase station '240V: yes' and never say that the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus and the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus cut their 240 V outlets while recharging from 120 V. This page lines up each maker's own statement on that condition, adds amps at 240 V, and so separates the units that can keep a well pump running through a long outage with generator top-ups.

page.title: Best 240V Portable Power Station (2026): Split-Phase Picks Compared
page.desc: Which power stations run 240 V appliances from one unit, and which keep their 240 V outlet live while recharging from 120 V. BLUETTI Apex 300, Anker SOLIX S5000, F3800 Plus and Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus compared by maker statements and amps at 240 V.
page.answer: Short answer. Power stations that can run 240 volt appliances from one unit include the BLUETTI Apex 300, Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus and Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus, but of those three only the Apex 300 keeps 240V split phase output live while it charges from 120V. Its limit is 16 A (3,840 W).

page.after:
What the differences mean

All four make 120/240 V split-phase power from one box with no second unit or hub. The 240 V outlet's label doesn't tell you how much current it can supply. The inverter does:

  • BLUETTI Apex 300: 3,840 W ÷ 240 V = 16 A. Its 14-50R is labelled 50 A, so it gives 16 ÷ 50 = 32% of the outlet's label. Adding a B300K battery ($2,599 for the bundle at BLUETTI, 2026-11-17) doubles the energy to 5,529.6 Wh but leaves the current at 16 A.
  • Anker SOLIX S5000: 4,500 W ÷ 240 V = 18.75 A.
  • Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus: Anker states 25 A on the L14-30R. 25 A × 240 V = 6,000 W, the whole inverter.
  • Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus: 7,200 W ÷ 240 V = 30 A on either 240 V outlet.
  • EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra (inverter + battery, $3,699 at EcoFlow, 2026-11-17): 7,200 W ÷ 240 V = 30 A. $3,699 ÷ 6.144 kWh = $602 per kWh. The DELTA Pro Ultra X bundle ($7,899) reaches 12,000 W ÷ 240 V = 50 A, but EcoFlow sells it as an installed system.

Cost per kWh for the pick: $1,499 ÷ 2.7648 kWh = $542 (BLUETTI store, 2026-11-17). StorageReview measured 2.39 kWh of AC out of the Apex 300, so a 3,000 W load runs about 2,390 ÷ 3,000 × 60 = 48 minutes.

Does 240 V stay on while the station recharges?

This matters most in a multi-day outage, when a well pump or other 240 V load has to keep running while you top the station up from a wall outlet or a 120 V generator.

  • Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus: its AC input is 120 V only (15 A max, 1,800 W charging, 1,440 W bypass), and Anker states that 240 V output 'cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC'. On a 120 V generator, Anker's FAQ says output is available on the L1 phase only, with 'no output when connected to the L2 phase'. 240 V pass-through of up to 6,000 W needs a 240 V generator and Anker's Generator Adapter.
  • Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus: its AC input is 120 V, 15 A, 1,750 W. Jackery's spec page lists '240V Ports: No Output' during simultaneous charge and discharge. In that state the 120 V ports are limited to 12 A in Backup UPS mode or 30 A in Online UPS mode.
  • BLUETTI Apex 300: BLUETTI states you can 'Charge the Apex 300 at 120V without interrupting 240V output'. StorageReview describes two inverters, one per line, with the 14-50R carrying both lines plus neutral and ground in 240 V mode. It measured a 16 ms switch from utility to battery.
  • Anker SOLIX S5000: The Gadgeteer (Vincent Nguyen) reports that 'the 240V output stays available while the station charges from a 120V source'. Anker's own S5000 page lists 1,800 W AC input at 120 V and 4,500 W at 240 V, and says nothing either way about 240 V output while charging.

{buy:bluetti-apex-300}

Not recommended

Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus for one-box 240 V: Jackery's store says a single unit runs 120 V appliances and you need to 'connect two units' for 240 V. Don't confuse it with the HomePower 3600 Pro Max. EcoFlow TITAN 5000 Classic: EcoFlow says it 'supports 120V output only'. For a 240 V load that must survive a long outage with 120 V recharging, also skip the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus, whose 240 V outlet shuts off while it charges. Buy it only if you will run 240 V on battery and need up to 25 A. Anker's US store showed it as sold out on 2026-11-17.
